answer: One identity stewards one heritage-listed historic house on a named knoll: the steward lives on site, logs monthly conservation work, opens the house. One house backs one identity only; a second claim is rejected, and a transfer voids it until the steward serves 90 days. The post costs 2,200 units plus 365 days of residence and repairs; 100 fakes cost 220,000 units, 100 houses, no fable shortens that year. Cheapest cheat: a stand-in hired for 1,500 units a season, but the stand-in burns their own one post, and the yearly zenith inspection checks log against house, so forgery revokes both.
